blame_rule: git blame -w -M -C --first-parent at the pinned commit; committer
time per line (a branch merged later is dated by its merge; moved
or copied lines keep their original date)
a question is 'after' when at least half of its key's non-blank
lines changed after the cutoff day (23:59:59 UTC)
key lines: locate = the function; callers = the call lines of
key callers and open disputes; flow = every candidate hop's

scope.code: every tracked .py under waku/ (hosted/, evals/, lab/, scripts/, examples/, docs/ excluded)

scoring.locate: file + function; a function nested inside the key function also counts
scoring.callers: the set of direct callers (file + function, or file + <module> for top-level code), under waku/
scoring.flow: the required hops Han marks, recalled, in order (LCS); hops in neither the trace nor the AST count as invented

flow_rules: keep: the subtree under the question's entry call(s), repo
calls only (the T3 filter: package source, no tests)
drop with callees: logging and metrics:
drop with callees: folded calls (fold = one hop, callees
drop, keep callees: generator re-entries (resume events);
a generator counts once, where it was created
drop, keep callees: trivial functions (one statement: a
return with no call, or a get_/is_/has_ return)
merge: a function called again counts once, at its first

ast_resolution.name: plain name: same-module function, nested function or import
ast_resolution.class: class called by name -> its __init__ (found up the repo bases)
ast_resolution.self: self.m() / cls.m() -> m on the class or its repo bases
ast_resolution.override: self.m() -> an override of m in a repo subclass (class hierarchy analysis)
ast_resolution.super: super().m() -> m on a repo base class
ast_resolution.module: module.f() on an imported repo module
ast_resolution.classattr: Class.m() on a repo class named in the code

dispute_kinds.attr: obj.m() on an object whose type the AST cannot see; m matches the target by name only
dispute_kinds.getattr: getattr(obj, 'm') with the target's name as a string
dispute_kinds.reference: the target passed or stored without being called (callback, registry, decorator)

questions.text: Before each later model call in a turn, where are long tool results the model has already read cut to their opening, with a note saying how long they were?
When a turn runs out of steps, where is the one last model call made with tool use switched off, so the reply comes from what was already gathered?
Where does a small model decide whether a message needs the user's stored memories at all, returning search keywords, and falling back to searching when its reply can't be read?

When chats are distilled into long-term facts, where is a proposed fact thrown out because it is about the assistant's own running condition, such as an account balance, a rate limit or a token count?
Where is a proposed fact dropped because it has a number or a date and every name, number and date in it already appears in the memory the turn read?

Where is the folder that holds the assistant's database and files chosen: an environment variable first, then an older per-folder location kept until the person copies it, otherwise one under the user's home directory?
Where does a workflow of steps run in waves, running the ready steps of a wave on a thread pool, merging what they return into one shared dictionary and raising if two write the same key?
Where is a user's free text reduced to lowercase word tokens joined by OR, so it can be used safely as a full-text search over the SQLite index?
Where are the stored how-to instructions picked for a message, by counting words it shares with each one's name and description, re-reading the folder first when a file changed?
Where is one action the model asked for run so that an unknown name or an exception comes back to the model as text instead of stopping the turn?
Where are the values of configured secrets (keys, tokens, passwords) removed from an error message before it is shown to the person in a chat app?
Where is a plugin hook's JSON answer read for extra context, a refusal of the action about to run, and a message to show the person?
